items.summary_orig: Some binary stars end up sharing a common envelope of gas, as the primary star draws material away from its companion. The envelope exerts drag on the stars and they can spiral toward each other. In some cases, this creates an eruption or explosion called a luminous red nova. For the first time, astronomers got to observe one of these in real time.

items.summary_orig: Humanity is quickly starting to saturate our ability to track all of the satellites we have in deep space. NASA’s Deep Space Network (DSN) has been the workhorse for tracking such things for decades, but is quickly being overwhelmed by the number of requests it receives.
